answer: Peers re-execute a random 5% of submitted work each epoch, and a job is split so no single auditor sees the whole result. Re-execution goes to a rotating set that excludes anyone who recruited the author, so no identity may audit its own recruit. A farm needs its clones to survive random spot checks by strangers, which means the work has to be real or the mismatch surfaces in one round. A farm's inlet of fake accounts gets no clean record, the ivory of a verified history takes months to build, and an island of clones cannot borrow it.
